City council approves new transit budget

The city council voted on Tuesday to approve a revised transit budget that increases funding for bus services across the metropolitan area, ending months of debate among members.

According to figures published by Reuters, ridership has grown steadily over the last two years, which supporters said justified the additional spending on new vehicles and drivers.

Opponents argued that the money would be better spent on road repairs, citing a report that was also covered by the Associated Press in its weekend coverage of local infrastructure.

The budget takes effect at the start of the next fiscal year, and the council will review spending quarterly, according to a statement released by the mayor's office after the vote.

Residents can read the full document on the city website or attend the next public meeting, where officials will answer questions about how the new funds will be allocated.
